newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower, rangebound trade expected.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower, rangebound trade expected.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled barely weaker and within their recent range as players prepared for an abbreviated and featureless week, market sources said.

Commission house buy stops carried the market to its high of 75.30 in March in early dealings, and trade selling capped the move up. March hovered close to unchanged throughout most of the session, dealers said.
March cotton settled 0.20 cent lower at 74.90 cents per pound, traded 75.30 to 74.80 cents. December ended down 0.31 at 73.33, while the deferred contracts settled 0.17 higher to 0.28 lower.
Open interest in the December contract fell 1,454 lots to 1,778 lots as of Friday. December 6 is the final trading day for the contract.
"We are pretty much looking at what the market is going to do for the next two days," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said of today's range.

NYCE will be closed Thursday and Friday due to Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday. Mill buying is also likely to be absent from this week's market as several plan to close early this week, industry sources said.
